completed_tasks.name: Seed and verify approved SQMS Opportunity and Bid transition metadata
Prove existing Workflow Start, Context, and Action APIs with live SQMS runtime scenarios

remaining_tasks.name: Design and mock console Start, Get Context, and Execute against the supplied SQMS Opportunity/Bid table identities

decisions.decision: Use the existing generic Workflow Start, Context, and Action surfaces for SQMS.
decisions.rationale: The live API proved that seeded metadata supplies role-filtered available actions and validates transitions without duplicate SQMS transition code.

decisions.decision: Do not change workflow-engine code for SQMS transition integration.
decisions.rationale: Opportunity and Bid representative paths ran successfully through the existing public APIs.

decisions.decision: Keep non-Completed terminal runtime-status handling deferred.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly deferred terminal synchronization to a broader later implementation.

decisions.decision: Protect both Portfolio Trade and current SQMS behavior as regression baselines for any generic-engine change.
decisions.rationale: The engine is shared by multiple applications and must remain generic and backward compatible.

decisions.decision: Use console scenarios/tests to mock the SQMS application boundary; UI is out of scope.
decisions.rationale: The supplied SQMS Bid and Opportunity tables define the application records, while this repository owns workflow integration proof rather than UI work.

next_action: Read .planning/SQMS-CONTEXT.md, inspect the actual cp_sharepoint SSQMS table schema details, and design a console-only Start, Get Context, and Execute proof without changing UI or adding deferred capabilities.
context_notes: Iteration 1 seeded 31 Opportunity and 9 Bid transitions. Iteration 2 made no engine code changes and proved live Start, Context, and Action behavior. The selected next capability is a console mock of the SQMS application boundary using the supplied Bid and Opportunity table shapes. UI, tasks, SLA, notifications, scheduling, aggregation, and terminal synchronization remain out of this iteration.
